newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 11 to 849 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 11 to 849 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 849 as of Nov. 15, up 11 from the prior week and 70 above the year-ago total of 779, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 10 to 716, while rigs working offshore rose three to 108. The number of rigs active in inland waters fell by two to 25.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Louisiana, which showed an increase of nine and New Mexico, which showed a decrease of five. Texas dipped by three.

A total of 366 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up 17 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by five to 481, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects dropped by one to two.
There were 198 rigs drilling directionally, 69 drilling horizontally and 582 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 12 to 323 versus 215 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said 165 rigs were under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Nov. 15, up one from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, was 92.2 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean rose one this week to 106 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count remained unchanged at 564 out of a total fleet of 605, making the utilization rate 93.2 percent.
